title: Euclidean–Lorentzian Dichotomy and Algebraic Causality in Finite Ring Continuum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$, with $(\p-1)/2$ squares and $(\p-1)/2$ nonsquares; $-1$ is a square for $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; $X^{2}-\nu$ is irreducible for a nonsquare $\nu$; the multiplicative group of $\F_{\p^{2}}$ is cyclic; every prime $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ is a sum of two squares (Fermat).

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Quadratic forms over finite fields of odd characteristic: nondegenerate forms are classified by dimension and discriminant, isotropic in dimension three and more; in dimension four the hyperbolic type ($|O_{4}^{+}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{2}-1)^{2}$) and the elliptic type ($|O_{4}^{-}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{4}-1)$); Witt's theorem; the Cartan--Dieudonné theorem, the orthogonal group generated by reflections in non-null vectors.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The framed Subject: the shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with frame $(\chron;0,1,\g)$ and quarter-turn $\im=-\g^{\kap}$; the drive $\g$ is a nonsquare on every shell, the time coefficient $\nu=\g$ canonical; the norm-one cycle as the non-split torus.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The continuum comparison: Minkowski's form $-c^{2}t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ of signature $(1,3)$ and Witt index one over $\R$, its Lorentz group $O(1,3)$; the ordering of $\R$ that finite fields lack.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The Carrier and the Subject: the Carrier a finite, timeless torsor of $\Om=4\dS+1$ points, $\Om$ prime, with no clock; a Subject a shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with $\p^{2}<\Om$, whose $\p^{2}$ register pairs $(t,x)$ of a time and a position reading the Carrier's points hold; on a Carrier of even capacity $2^{-1}\equiv2\dS+1$ has a root $c$, a Carrier constant.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Time and the arrow: time is the drive; the drift of the embedded Subject against the Carrier is one-directional on every registrable duration, since $\p^{2}<\Om$; the record gains one count per chronon and none recurs, the second law of the record.

blocks.title: The causal reading and the window

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: Causality is algebraic and lives on the Subject's shell: the time axis carries the drive's nonsquare class, the null cone and the two non-null classes are its invariant separation (B7), the boosts the non-split torus (C2); the root $\eta$ lives in the pair algebra, never in a further shell; the arrow is the drift (A6). Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate:
Local correspondence [chart]: with $
u$ read as its least positive representative and $(
u+3)R^{2}<\p$, integer points bounded by $R$ satisfy $Q_{
u}=0$ in $\Z$ iff on the shell (the window law, 1:D8); the correspondence holds for every small coefficient and does not see the square class.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: The window is sharp: no integer point with coordinates bounded by $R$, where $3R^{2}<\p$ and $\g R^{2}<\p$, is a null point of the shell off the real cone; for $\p=a^{2}+b^{2}$, $0<a\le b$, the point $(0,a,b,0)$ is one, so the least such half-width $R_{\star}$ has $\p\le\max(\g,3)R_{\star}^{2}$ and $R_{\star}\le b<\sqrt{\p}$.
rows.name: window_sharpness

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: The temporal fibres: above each nonzero pair $(t,x)$ the null cone of $Q_{\g}$ has $\p-1$ points, above the origin $2\p-1$; the null cone spreads evenly over the temporal plane.
rows.name: temporal_fibres

B2.name: FRC.Causality.no_causal_root
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, first clause): `c² = ν` makes `ν` a square, so a nonsquare `ν` has no root.

B2.name: FRC.Causality.neg_sq_is_square
B2.doc: 3:B2 (the consequence): when `−1` is a square (`card F ≢ 3 mod 4`) so is `−c²`, and every coefficient of `−c² t² + x² + y² + z²` lies in the class of squares — a Euclidean form for every `c ≠ 0`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.no_causal_root
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, first clause) — `c² = ν` makes `ν` a square, so a nonsquare `ν` has no root `c`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.neg_sq_is_square
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, the consequence) — `−c²` is a square on every shell: `−c² = (i·c)²` with `i² = −1`; so with `c ≠ 0` every coefficient of `−c² t² + x² + y² + z²` is a square and the form is Euclidean.

B3.name: FRC.Causality.absorb
B3.doc: 3:B3 (Lemma absorption): coefficients `a_i = w_i² a_0` are absorbed by `x_i ↦ w_i x_i`.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.absorb
B3.doc: 3:B3 (Lemma absorption) — if `a_i = w_i² a_0` for `i = 1, 2, 3` then `a_0 x_0² + a_1 x_1² + a_2 x_2² + a_3 x_3² = a_0 (x_0² + (w_1 x_1)² + (w_2 x_2)² + (w_3 x_3)²)`: a common square class is absorbed by the rescaling `x_i ↦ w_i x_i`, with no square root of `a_0` itself required.

B4.name: FRC.Causal.null_elliptic
B4.doc: 3:B4, 3:B7 — the null cone of `Q_ν` for a nonsquare `ν`: `p³ − p² + p` points, the elliptic count (written `N + p² = p³ + p`).

B4.name: FRC.Causal.null_hyperbolic
B4.doc: 3:B4, 3:B2 — the null cone of `Q_ν` for a square `ν = w²`, `w ≠ 0`: `p³ + p² − p` points, the hyperbolic count (written `N + p = p³ + p²`).

B4.name: FRC.Causal.plane_zero_aniso
B4.doc: 3:B4 — for a nonsquare `ν` the plane `x² − ν t²` vanishes only at the origin: one point.

B4.name: FRC.Causal.plane_zero_split
B4.doc: 3:B4 — for a square `ν = w²`, `w ≠ 0`, the plane `x² − w² t²` vanishes on `2p − 1` points: the two lines `x = ±wt`.

B5.name: FRC.Causality.aniso_tx
B5.doc: 3:B5: `x² − ν t²` is anisotropic for a nonsquare `ν`.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.aniso_tx
B5.doc: 3:B5 — the plane `x² − ν t²` is anisotropic when `ν` is a nonsquare: `x² = ν t²` forces `t = x = 0` (else `ν = (x/t)²`). This is the Witt kernel of the Lorentzian form, its index one.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null_yz
B5.doc: 3:B5 — the `(y, z)`-plane `y² + z²` is hyperbolic on every shell: `(1, i)` is null.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null_tx_of_square
B5.doc: 3:B5 — for a square `ν = w²` the `(t, x)`-plane is hyperbolic too: `(1, w)` is null; the form is then `H ⊥ H`, Witt index two — the Euclidean type.

B6.name: FRC.Causal.sphere_drive
B6.doc: 3:B6 — for the drive `g` every nonzero value of `Q_g = −g t² + x² + y² + z²` is taken `p³ + p` times; at `a = −g` this is the time sphere, whose `p³ + p` points times `|O(3, 𝔽_p)| = 2p(p² − 1)` give `|O₄⁻(p)| = 2p²(p⁴ − 1)`.

B6.name: FRC.Causal.plane_nonzero
B6.doc: 3:C2, 3:B6 — for the drive `g` the plane `x² − g t²` takes every nonzero value `p + 1` times: the norm-one cycle of `𝔽_p(√g)` (the boosts, `γ² − g b² = 1`) has `p + 1` elements.

B7.name: FRC.Causal.similitude
B7.doc: 3:B7 — the similitude `(t, x, y, z) ↦ (cz, ax − by, bx + ay, cνt)` with `a² + b² = ν` and `c² = −1` multiplies `Q_ν = −ν t² + x² + y² + z²` by `ν`.

B7.name: FRC.Causal.class_flip
B7.doc: 3:B7 — multiplication by the drive exchanges the two square classes of the nonzero residues.

B7.name: FRC.Causal.null_elliptic
B7.doc: 3:B4, 3:B7 — the null cone of `Q_ν` for a nonsquare `ν`: `p³ − p² + p` points, the elliptic count (written `N + p² = p³ + p`).

B8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.norm_mul
B8.doc: 3:B8 — the norm is multiplicative: `N((a + b√ν)(c + d√ν)) = N(a + b√ν) N(c + d√ν)`, i.e. `(ac + νbd)² − ν(ad + bc)² = (a² − νb²)(c² − νd²)` — the identity behind every boost.

B8.name: FRC.Causal.drive_meets_norm_one
B8.doc: 3:B8 — the drive cycle `𝔽_p^×` meets the norm-one cycle of `𝔽_p(√ν)` in `±1`: `γ² − ν·0² = 1` forces `γ = ±1`.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_preserves
C2.doc: 3:C2 (the finite Lorentz boost): `Λ(γ, b) = !![γ, b; νb, γ]` with `γ² − νb² = 1` preserves `x² − ν t²`.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_comp
C2.doc: 3:C2: the boosts compose as the norm-one elements of `F(√ν)` multiply.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_orthogonal
C2.doc: 3:C2: `Λ(γ, b)` is orthogonal for the Gram matrix `diag(−ν, 1)` of `Q_ν`: `Λᵀ G Λ = G`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.boost_preserves
C2.doc: 7:A10, 3:C2, 8:D14 (the finite Lorentz boost) — with `γ² − νb² = 1`, `Λ(γ, b)` preserves `x² − ν t²` exactly, on every shell.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.boost_comp_t
C2.doc: 7:A10, 3:C2, 8:D15 — boosts compose as their parameters multiply in `K`: `Λ(γ₁, b₁) Λ(γ₂, b₂) = Λ(γ₁γ₂ + νb₁b₂, γ₁b₂ + b₁γ₂)`, the `t`-row.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.norm_one_mul
C2.doc: 7:A10, 3:C2, 8:D15 — the norm-one elements form a group: `N(z₁z₂) = N(z₁)N(z₂) = 1`.

C2.name: FRC.Causal.plane_nonzero
C2.doc: 3:C2, 3:B6 — for the drive `g` the plane `x² − g t²` takes every nonzero value `p + 1` times: the norm-one cycle of `𝔽_p(√g)` (the boosts, `γ² − g b² = 1`) has `p + 1` elements.

C3.name: FRC.Causality.gamma_ne_zero
C3.doc: 3:C3: `γ ≠ 0` on every boost of the Lorentzian plane (`γ = 0` would make `ν = (i/b)²`).

C3.name: FRC.Causality.gamma_velocity
C3.doc: 3:C3: the velocity `v = −νb/γ` satisfies `γ² (ν − v²) = ν` — `γ = 1/√(1 − β²)` with `β² = v²/ν`.

C3.name: FRC.Causality.velocity_addition
C3.doc: 3:C3 (Einstein's addition law, exact): `v₁₂ (ν + v₁v₂) = ν (v₁ + v₂)`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gamma_ne_zero
C3.doc: 3:C3 — `γ ≠ 0` on every boost of the Lorentzian plane: `γ = 0` would give `ν b² = −1`, i.e. `ν = (i/b)²`, a square.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gamma_velocity
C3.doc: 3:C3 — the velocity of the boost, `v = −νb/γ` (`vγ = −νb`), satisfies `γ² (ν − v²) = ν`: the finite form of `γ = 1/√(1 − β²)` with `β² = v²/ν`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.velocity_addition
C3.doc: 3:C3 (the velocity addition law) — for boosts with velocities `v₁, v₂` (`v_i γ_i = −ν b_i`) and the composed boost's velocity `v₁₂`, `v₁₂ (ν + v₁v₂) = ν (v₁ + v₂)`: Einstein's law `v₁₂ = (v₁ + v₂)/(1 + v₁v₂/ν)`, exact.

C4.name: FRC.Causal.xboost_preserves
C4.doc: 3:C4 — the `x`-boost `Λ ⊕ I₂` lies in `O(Q_ν, 𝔽_p)` on every shell: it preserves `x² − ν t² + y² + z²`.

C4.name: FRC.Causal.square_shift
C4.doc: 3:C4 — the square shift: for `t ≠ 0` the residue `x = (1 + g t²)/2` makes `x² − g t²` the nonzero square `y²`, `y = (g t² − 1)/2`; `y ≠ 0` since `g t² = 1` would make the drive a square.

C4.name: FRC.Causal.boost_transitive
C4.doc: 3:C4 — the boosts act transitively on each level set of the plane `x² − g t² = m`, `m ≠ 0`: the boost `γ = (x₂x₁ − g t₂t₁)/m`, `b = (t₂x₁ − x₂t₁)/m` (the quotient of the two points in `𝔽_p(√g)`) carries `(t₁, x₁)` to `(t₂, x₂)`.

C4.name: FRC.Causal.time_to_space
C4.doc: 3:C4 — time to space: for `t ≠ 0` there are a residue `x` and a boost carrying `(t, x)` to `(0, y)` with `y ≠ 0`. With the spatial rotations, which give the spatial part any `x`-component (Witt), every non-null vector of `Q_g` is carried to a spatial one; the conjugates of the spatial reflections are then all the reflections, which generate `O(Q_g, 𝔽_p)` (Cartan–Dieudonné).

D1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null13
D1.doc: 7:A8, 3:B4, 3:D1 [value] — the null cone of `Q_2` on `𝔽₁₃` has `2041 = 13³ − 13² + 13` points: the elliptic type.

D1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.euclid13
D1.doc: 7:A8, 3:B4, 3:D1 [value] — the Euclidean form (`ν = 1`) on `𝔽₁₃` has `2353 = 13³ + 13² − 13` zeros: the hyperbolic type.

D1.name: FRC.Causal.shell173
D1.doc: 3:D1 [value] — `𝔽₁₇₃`, drive `2`: the null cone of `Q_2` has `173³ − 173² + 173 = 5 147 961` points and the boosts number `174`, from the general counts on the frame `(τ; 0, 1, 2)`.

E3.name: FRC.Causality.window_ghost_exists
E3.doc: 3:E3 — a box off the window (the theorem lives in the extension theme).

E3.name: FRC.Causal.window_exact
E3.doc: 3:E3 — no point off the real cone inside the window. Read an integer point `(t, x, y, z)` through the absolute values of its coordinates, each at most `R`, with `3R² < p` and `νR² < p`. If `x² + y² + z² ≡ ν t² (mod p)`, that is `Q_ν ≡ 0`, then `x² + y² + z² = ν t²`: the point lies on the real cone of the integral form.

E3.name: FRC.Causal.window_ghost
E3.doc: 3:E3 — the window is sharp below `√p`. When `p = a² + b²` with `a > 0`, the point `(t, x, y, z) = (0, a, b, 0)` satisfies `x² + y² + z² ≡ ν t² (mod p)` but not `x² + y² + z² = ν t²`: a null point of the shell off the real cone, with coordinates at most `b` and `b² < p`.

E4.name: FRC.Causal.temporal_fiber
E4.doc: 3:E4 — the null cone over the temporal plane: above each pair `(t, x)` lie `p − 1` null points of `Q_g`, and `2p − 1` above the origin, since the plane `x² − g t²` vanishes only at the origin.
